keyVerseText: And Moses said, This shall be, when the LORD shall give you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full; for that the LORD heareth your murmurings which ye murmur against him: and what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against the LORD.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb שָׂבַע (sâbaʻ) is a primitive root word that fundamentally conveys the idea of being filled or satisfied, especially in a physical or figurative sense. Its core meaning revolves around having enough or being full to the point of contentment, whether with food or other desires. This root sense enriches the English gloss by emphasizing not just fullness but a state of sufficiency and satisfaction that can extend beyond the literal to emotional or spiritual fulfillment.
usageInScripture: Throughout Scripture, שָׂבַע appears 96 times and is predominantly translated as expressions related to satisfaction and fullness, such as 'shall be satisfied,' 'and be satisfied,' and 'filled.' This consistent usage reveals a semantic range focused on both physical satiation and metaphorical fulfillment. The verb appears in various forms, including Qal and Piel stems, indicating both the state of being satisfied and the action of satisfying, highlighting its versatile role in describing human and divine provision.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, שָׂבַע underscores God's provision and the human experience of satisfaction that comes from Him. It reflects the biblical truth that God is the ultimate source who fills and satisfies the needs of His people, both physically and spiritually. This verb reminds believers that true contentment is found in God's blessings and that He listens to and responds to human needs. It also warns against the weariness or surfeiting that can come from excess, pointing to the balance God ordains. In Christ, this fulfillment is perfected, as He satisfies the deepest hunger of the soul.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 16:8 states, 'This shall be, when the LORD shall give you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full,' emphasizing God's faithful provision that will satisfy His people. The use of שָׂבַע here highlights the completeness and sufficiency of God's sustenance, reassuring the Israelites that their physical needs will be met fully. It also frames their murmuring as misplaced, since the Lord is the one who truly satisfies, not Moses or Aaron. This verse invites trust in God's provision, assuring believers today that He hears and answers their needs with fullness.
